newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: HORSE RACING-DORANS PRIDE BACK TO BEST.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-DORANS PRIDE BACK TO BEST.

text.p: Former Cheltenham champion Dorans Pride continued his rehabilitation after serious illness had threatened his life when he landed the Grade One Drinmore Novice Steeplechase at Fairyhouse on Sunday.

Last December Doran's Pride required emergency treatment after he had succumbed to a bout of colic but the seven-year-old gelding recovered and he has won all three of his outings over fences this season.
"It's a miracle really," said County Limerick-based trainer Michael Hourigan. "I thought he was dead., but he's a tough old horse as he showed in the race."

The 5-4 favourite, ridden by Richard Dunwoody, edged out Tony McCoy on See More Business (5-2), trained by Paul Nicholls in Britain, by a length in an exciting finish to the two and a half mile (4-km) contest.
Hourigan said his stable star will probably be entered for the Cheltenham Gold Cup but the gelding is more likely to go for the Stayers Hurdle, a race he won in style in 1995.

Nicholls said he would like See More Business to take the winner on again at Cheltenham. "I'll take him on again any time. They are two serious horses," Nicholls said. "I would have liked the ground to have been a bit softer."
Ireland's equine star, Danoli, winner of the top novice hurdle race at Cheltenham and another at Aintree in 1994, was a faller at the third fence in this race.

Danoli was not hurt and trainer Tom Foley schooled the gelding over nine fences after the last of seven races on the card had been completed. "He's fine, he just made a stupid mistake," Foley said of his fall in the race.

English raider Large Action, ridden by Jamie Osborne, landed the Grade One Hatton's Grace Hurdle and was immediately installed as 5-1 second favourite behind Alderbrook (3-1) for the Champion Hurdle in Cheltenham next March.
Earlier, seven times Irish champion jump jockey Charlie Swan had ridden Aidan O'Brien-trained Istabraq, the 11-8 favourite, to an easy victory in another grade one hurdle event.
O'Brien said the winner would be aimed for one of the top novice hurdles at Cheltenham.
